body.statement:
Let \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), \(M_1>0\), and \(M_2>M_1^2\) be fixed, and let \(\delta_T\ge0\) be any deterministic sequence with \(\delta_T\to0\).  With \(\beta=2/(2+t_0\zeta)\), there are constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{loc}}\le C_{\mathrm{loc}}<\infty\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(T\),
\[
 c_{\mathrm{loc}}\left\{T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}\delta_T^{2(1-\beta)}\right\}
 \le R_T(t_0,\zeta,1+\delta_T)
 \le C_{\mathrm{loc}}\left\{T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}\delta_T^{2(1-\beta)}\right\}.
\]
An attaining observable estimator is \(\widehat\theta_{\kappa_T}\), where \(\kappa_T=0\) if \(T\delta_T^2\le1\), and otherwise
\[
 \kappa_T:=\min\!\left\{\left\lfloor T/2\right\rfloor,
 \left\lfloor\frac{\log(T\delta_T^2)}{2\log(1/\alpha)+\log L}\right\rfloor\right\}.
\]
Thus the exact threshold is \(\delta_T\asymp T^{-1/2}\): when \(T\delta_T^2=O(1)\), immediate weighting has parametric order, whereas when \(T\delta_T^2\to\infty\), the required history is of order \(\log(T\delta_T^2)\) and the second risk term dominates.  There is no logarithmic factor in the risk.
body.proof_tex:
We derive the stated shrinking-overlap result from the stronger uniform theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\text{-}overlap\text{-}frontier}\).  Put \(C_T:=1+\delta_T\).  Then
\[
 q_{C_T}=\frac{\delta_T}{1+\delta_T}. \tag{38}
\]
Because \(\delta_T\to0\), for all sufficiently large \(T\) one has \(0\le\delta_T\le1\), and hence
\[
 \frac12\delta_T\le q_{C_T}\le\delta_T. \tag{39}
\]
Raising (39) to the positive power \(2(1-\beta)\) and applying the uniform theorem proves both displayed risk inequalities in the target statement, after changing only constants depending on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\).

It remains to verify the particular \(\delta_T\)-based tuning displayed in the target, since the uniform theorem uses \(q_{C_T}\).  Write
\[
 x_\delta:=T\delta_T^2,
 \qquad x_q:=Tq_{C_T}^2.
\]
By (39), \(x_q\le x_\delta\le4x_q\).  If \(x_\delta\le1\), the displayed estimator takes depth zero, and \(\mathrm{lem{:}radius\text{-}sensitive\text{-}phiw\text{-}envelope}\) gives order \(T^{-1}\).  If \(x_\delta>1\), put
\[
 k_\delta:=\min\!\left\{\left\lfloor T/2\right\rfloor,
 \left\lfloor\frac{\log x_\delta}{2\log(1/\alpha)+\log L}\right\rfloor\right\}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\), the cap is inactive because \(x_\delta\le T\) eventually.  The same floor calculation as in (12)--(13), using \(q_{C_T}\le\delta_T\), gives
\[
 q_{C_T}^2\alpha^{2k_\delta}
 \le \alpha^{-2}T^{-\beta}\delta_T^{2(1-\beta)},
 \qquad
 T^{-1}L^{k_\delta}
 \le T^{-\beta}\delta_T^{2(1-\beta)}. \tag{40}
\]
If the exceptional regime \(x_\delta>1\ge x_q\) occurs, then \(x_\delta\le4\), so \(k_\delta\) is bounded by a constant depending only on \(t_0,\zeta\); the envelope is again of order \(T^{-1}\).  Thus the estimator stated in the target attains its upper rate in every case.

The ratio of its second risk term to \(T^{-1}\) is \((T\delta_T^2)^{1-\beta}\).  Since \(0<\beta<1\), this proves the stated threshold and dominance claims.  The geometric variance calculation in the envelope proves that no logarithmic factor is introduced.
body.justification: This local statement is the \(C_T=1+\delta_T\) specialization of the stronger uniform overlap-frontier theorem.
body.gap: The former draft treated the shrinking-radius transition as open; the uniform modulus and radius-sensitive PHIW envelope now close it.
body.consumer: Near stationary equality, it converts a substantive occupancy assurance into the exact \(T^{-1/2}\) threshold for using immediate rather than growing-history weights.
